body_ar:
حكم الاستغاثة بغير الله

ما حكم الاستغاثة بغير الله ولو كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم؟

أن الله تعالى يقول في كتابه: {ذلكم الله ربكم له الملك، والذين تدعون من دونه ما يملكون من قطمير، إن تدعوهم لا يسمعوا دعاءكم ولو سمعوا ما استجابوا لكم ويوم القيامة يكفرون بشرككم ولا ينبئك مثل خبير}

فلا يمكن أن يخبرك أحد أعلم من الله عز وجل وقد أخبرك بهذا الحكم الفاصل الذي أتى على كل الاحتمالات، فالاستغاثة أي طلب الغوث لا يمكن أن تتم إلا بالله عز وجل فهو المغيث وحده، ومن سواه لا يملك لنفسه ولا لغيره نفعا ولا ضرا ولا موتا ولا حياة ولا نشورا، {وإن يسلبهم الذباب شيئا لا يستنقذوه منه ضعف الطالب والمطلوب ما قدروا الله حق قدره}.

----------------------------------------------------------------

حكم الذهاب إلى الكهان

هل الذهاب إلى الكهان أو إلى العرافين للدواء جائز أم لا؟

لا، وقد صح عن النبي (ص) النهي عن ذلك وبيان خطره فقال: من صدق كاهنا أو منجما أو عرافا فقد كفر بما أنزل على محمد، وجاء فيه أيضا عدم قبول أربعين صلاة أنه لا تقبل له أربعون صلاة،

ولذلك على الإنسان أن لا يتطلع على الغيب، وأن لا يخالط الذين يتطلعون عليه، وبالأخص في زماننا هذا، فهذا الزمان زمان الفتن، ونحن الآن ننتظر المسيح الدجال أن يأتي ، وهو شر غائب ينتظر، وما بين خلق آدم وقيام الساعة فتنة هي أعظم من فتنة المسيح الدجال، وما من نبي إلا وأنذره قومه وإن نوحا أنذره قومه،

والمسيح الدجال يبرئ الأكمه والأبرص ويحيي الموتى، يقتل الرجل فيشقه نصفين ويمشي بينهما ثم يناديه فيقوم وما به أثر، ويجري الله على يديه من الخوارق الشيء الكثير،

فلذلك على الناس أن يعلموا أن جريان الخوارق على يد إنسان إذا لم يكن من أهل الاستقامة والصلاح لا يغر، فإنه يجري على يد المسيح الدجال أكبر منه، فيمر على القرية الخربة فتتبعه كنوزها كيعاسيب النحل، ويمر على القوم مسنتين فيصدقونه فيأمر السماء فتمطر والأرض فتنبت، فتروح عليهم ماشيتهم أسبل ما كانت ضروعا، ويمر على قوم مخصبين فيكذبونه فيأمر السماء فتمسك ويأمر الأرض فتقحط فتروح عليهم ماشيتهم في شدة اللأواء فهذا من الخوارق التي تظهر على يديه،

وإذا عرفنا ذلك عرفنا أن هذه الخوارق حتى ولو كان فيها إخبار ببعض المغيبات فهي فتنة وعلى الإنسان أن يحذر منها، وقد بين النبي (ص) أنه سيخرج بين يدي الدجال ثلاثون دجالا كلهم يزعم أنه نبي.
body_en:
The ruling on seeking rescue from other than God

What is the ruling on seeking rescue from other than God, even if it be the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace?

God, exalted, says in His Book: {That is God, your Lord; to Him belongs the dominion. And those you call upon besides Him do not possess so much as the skin of a date stone. If you call upon them they do not hear your call, and if they heard they would not respond to you; and on the Day of Resurrection they will disown your having associated them with God. And none can inform you like One who is All-Aware} (Sūrat Fāṭir 35:13–14).

No one can inform you who is more knowing than God, mighty and majestic, and He has informed you of this decisive ruling, which has covered every possibility. Seeking rescue — that is, asking to be rescued — cannot be accomplished except by God, mighty and majestic, for He alone is the Rescuer; and whoever is other than Him possesses, for himself or for anyone else, no benefit and no harm, no death and no life and no raising up: {And if the fly should take something from them, they could not retrieve it from it. Weak are the seeker and the sought. They have not appraised God with the appraisal due to Him} (Sūrat al-Ḥajj 22:73–74).

----------------------------------------------------------------

The ruling on going to soothsayers

Is going to soothsayers, or to diviners, for a remedy permissible or not?

No. It is soundly established from the Prophet, upon whom be peace, that he forbade that and made clear its danger, for he said: 'Whoever believes a soothsayer, or an astrologer, or a diviner has disbelieved in what was sent down upon Muhammad.' And it has also come concerning it that forty prayers are not accepted — that forty prayers of his are not accepted.

For that reason a person must not seek to look into the unseen, and must not mix with those who seek to look into it — and especially in this time of ours, for this age is the age of trials. We are now waiting for the False Messiah to come, and he is an absent evil that is awaited. Between the creation of Adam and the rising of the Hour there is no trial greater than the trial of the False Messiah. There is no prophet but that he warned his people of him, and Noah warned his people of him.

The False Messiah heals the one born blind and the leper, and brings the dead to life: he kills a man, splitting him into two halves, and walks between them; then he calls him and he stands up with no mark upon him. God brings about at his hands a great many things that break the customary order.

Therefore people must know that the occurrence of such things at the hand of a person, if he is not of the people of uprightness and righteousness, is not to be taken in by, for greater than that occurs at the hand of the False Messiah. He passes by the ruined village and its treasures follow him like swarms of bees. He passes by a people in drought and they believe him, so he commands the sky and it rains, and the earth and it brings forth growth, and their livestock come home to them in the evening with their udders hanging fuller than they have ever been. And he passes by a people in plenty and they call him a liar, so he commands the sky and it withholds, and commands the earth and it suffers drought, and their livestock come home to them in the severest hardship. This is of the things that appear at his hands which break the customary order.

And if we know that, we know that these things — even if they include the reporting of some matters of the unseen — are a trial, and a person must beware of them. The Prophet, upon whom be peace, made clear that thirty impostors will come forth before the Dajjal, each one of them claiming to be a prophet.

flags.arabic: ما حكم الاستغاثة بغير الله ولو كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم؟
flags.context: the first item as a whole
options: publish with a preface from the Sheikh's office
hold from publication pending the Sheikh's office
publish as an ordinary item in the creed series
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW ADVISED (style guide §12). istighāthah through the Prophet or through the righteous is one of the sharpest fault lines between Muslim tendencies, and the questioner raises it in exactly those terms. The Sheikh answers with two Qur'anic passages and a categorical statement, and does not distinguish the cases that the discussion usually turns on — asking the dead directly, asking a living person for what he can do, tawassul through a person's standing. It has been translated exactly as given, with nothing added to soften or extend it, and with no qualifications introduced that he did not make.

flags.arabic: من صدق كاهنا أو منجما أو عرافا فقد كفر بما أنزل على محمد
options: has disbelieved in what was sent down upon Muhammad
has rejected what was revealed to Muhammad
has committed unbelief in what was revealed to Muhammad
flags.note: The Sheikh grades this report as soundly established from the Prophet but names no collection. The clause فقد كفر is a formula of severe censure whose legal force is debated in the tradition; the English keeps the literal wording rather than resolving it either into technical apostasy or into mere rebuke, since the Sheikh does not resolve it. Note that he answers the questioner's 'permissible or not?' with a bare 'No' and does not himself use the words ḥarām or makrūh.

flags.arabic: وجاء فيه أيضا عدم قبول أربعين صلاة
flags.context: وجاء فيه أيضا عدم قبول أربعين صلاة أنه لا تقبل له أربعون صلاة
options: his prayers are not accepted for forty days
his prayer is not accepted for forty nights
flags.note: The received wording of this report is 'his prayer is not accepted for forty nights'. The Sheikh gives it here as a count of forty prayers, and repeats it in that form. His wording has been kept rather than corrected to the familiar version, per style guide §11. Compare article 526 of this slice, where he gives the same report as 'forty days'.

flags.context: فتروح عليهم ماشيتهم أسبل ما كانت ضروعا
options: with their udders hanging fuller than they have ever been
with their udders at their most pendulous
with their udders at their fullest
flags.note: SOURCE VARIATION. The same clause reads أسمن ('fattest') in articles 522 and 538 of this slice and أسبل ('most pendulous') here. Both occur in transmissions of the hadith. The source reading has been followed in each article rather than standardised; a reviewer should decide whether to unify them.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

Two separate fatwas are published on this one page, divided in the source by a rule of hyphens. The rule is preserved in both body_ar and body_en; the site should render them as two separate items. Each item's own heading is part of the source text and has been kept.

Both Qur'anic quotations in the first item are given in the source within its own braces and without references; the references have been supplied in the English per house style and the Arabic has not been altered.
قطمير is the thin skin over a date stone, the proverbial smallest thing; it is rendered literally so the image survives.
The description of the Dajjal here overlaps with articles 522 and 538 of this slice, with small differences of wording in each. Each has been translated from its own text rather than harmonised.

ثلاثون دجالا is rendered 'thirty impostors' rather than 'thirty Dajjals', since the Arabic uses the common noun for the false claimants and the proper name for the one awaited, and English cannot carry both with one word.
